answer: Require merged-code provenance before payout. A newcomer submits 30 merged pull requests over 90 days, across three independent projects, including a cedar-mapping tool and a glacier-monitoring library. Maintainers from two different projects confirm each merge was real, reviewed work. Full payouts unlock only then, capped at $100 a week for a month. Forging 1,000 fakes means fabricating 30,000 credible merges and fooling 2,000 reviewers, costing over $400,000 and 90 days. The climb to the summit is slow, like a glacier carving a valley, leaving proof no shortcut can fake.
